## How it works

- [statement] GoBind asks for quantity, stock weight, colour/coating, deadline and destination ZIP when quoting cutting work. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://gobindery.com/capabilities/cutting
- [statement] GoBind says it can receive pieces printed elsewhere, count them and gather them in the requested order. This establishes a trade-finishing option when collation is outsourced. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://gobindery.com/capabilities/collating
- [statement] Smartpress advises against Soft Touch laminate for playing cards because it can make shuffling harder; a finish marketed for tactile appeal is therefore not automatically suitable for a game deck. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://smartpress.com/support/product-faq/collated-printing-faq

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] In a 2025 PrintPlanet discussion, operator tngcas attributed a sheet-walking problem to rollers needing replacement and said cleaning did not fix it. Treat this as an operator report, not a failure-rate or maintenance-cost estimate. (low confidence) — https://printplanet.com/threads/duplo-dc-618-skewing-in-machine.295010/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Xerox’s October 2017 iGen Thick Stock Capability sheet says simplex printing generally allows more sheet-size flexibility than duplex. For outsourced press work, confirm the actual duplex sheet format rather than assuming a simplex stock capability applies to two-sided cards. (low confidence) — https://www.xerox.com/digital-printing/latest/IG4DS-06U.PDF
- [statement] Bleed advice differs across the sources: ADL gives quarter-inch bleed advice, while Smartpress specifies 0.125 inch. Use the selected printer’s job-specific instructions rather than treating either allowance as universal. (medium confidence) — https://adlinteractive.com/category/tooling-up · keywords: Local commercial trade printing for game decks · also: https://smartpress.com/support/printing-basics/cutting-tolerance-for-print

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The World of Playing Cards describes Elaine Lewis outsourcing printed card sheets, then hand-colouring, cutting and boxing the packs herself; this is an example of a hybrid workflow, not a throughput benchmark. (low confidence) — https://www.wopc.co.uk/otc/production-methods
- [statement] Printworks describes imposition as multiple copies on each sheet and says reducing sheet passes lowers click charges; this supports comparing sheet layouts before estimating outsourced press costs. (low confidence) — https://www.chicagoprintworks.com/resource-posts/imposition-printing
- [statement] GoBind requires sheets with trim marks and a layout for cutting; arrange the finishing layout before handing off sheets. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://gobindery.com/capabilities/cutting
- [statement] Duplo’s DC-618 specification lists a maximum of 23 sheets per minute and a paper-weight range of 110–400 gsm. This is a manufacturer sheet-processing rating; it does not measure completed game decks, corner rounding, collation or packing. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-618-slitter-cutter-creaser/
- [statement] Duplo says the DC-618 reads sheet registration marks to compensate for shrinkage and image shift. Specify registration marks and finishing layout with the finishing operator before releasing outsourced press sheets. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.duplousa.com/product/dc-618-slitter-cutter-creaser/
- [statement] ADL Interactive describes a hybrid prototype route: outsource double-sided sheet printing to a local printer, then cut and sleeve the cards. Its account concerns prototypes or personal decks; it does not establish retail-deck quality or measured production throughput. (low confidence) — https://adlinteractive.com/category/tooling-up
- [statement] Smartpress says collated sets ship unseparated if neither stapling nor shrink wrapping is selected. A quote for collated printing therefore needs an explicit set-separation and bundling instruction. (low confidence) — https://smartpress.com/support/product-faq/collated-printing-faq
- [statement] Smartpress recommends allowing up to 0.125 inch trim variation, keeping essential content more than 0.125 inch inside the finished edge, and adding 0.125 inch bleed for edge-to-edge artwork. These are this supplier’s artwork allowances, not a universal playing-card registration specification. (low confidence) — https://smartpress.com/support/printing-basics/cutting-tolerance-for-print
- [statement] Lassco Wizer’s corner-cutter instructions say heavier material may be best cut only one or a few pieces at a time. Do not transfer a paper-stack capacity claim directly to heavy game-card stock. (low confidence) — https://www.lasscowizer.com/cmsb/uploads/cr-20-acco-instructions.pdf
- [statement] Lassco Wizer’s corner-cutter instructions identify material creeping and accumulated clippings that restrict blade travel, and specify occasional oil on the lever hinge screws. In-house corner finishing retains handling and maintenance work after the press work is outsourced. (low confidence) — https://www.lasscowizer.com/cmsb/uploads/cr-20-acco-instructions.pdf
- [statement] PRINTING United Alliance presents GRACoL as guidelines and color tools for print buyers, designers and suppliers. It provides a concrete color-specification reference to discuss with a local supplier. (low confidence) — https://www.printing.org/library/standards/specifications-for-print-production
- [statement] Keskes Printing lists a press hold-up tariff of $58.00 per hour for delays caused by incorrect supply of a job to the printer. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.keskes.com/trade_services
- [statement] Game designer Jacob Vander Ende's A La Carte Manufacturing account on Game Design Skills assigns the creator the work of identifying, contacting and using suppliers and other business partners. His examples include local printing of card sheets followed by the creator cutting, laminating and packing them. (low confidence) — https://gamedesignskills.com/game-development/how-to-make-a-board-game/
- [statement] Keskes Printing’s trade-services tariff states that its regular prices will be doubled on weekends. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.keskes.com/trade_services
